chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Musa ibn al-Hasan and Ahmad ibn Hilal from Musa ibn al-Qasim from 'Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about a musk mouse that is with a man while he is praying, and it is with him in his pocket or clothes, so he said, 'There is no objection to that.'

key_terms.فَأْرَةِ الْمِسْكِ: Musk mouse (a small rodent known for its scent)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does the presence of a mouse in one's pocket or clothing invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) is applied to minor impurities or creatures within clothing, confirming that the presence of a musk mouse does not invalidate the prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between major impurities (*najis*) that require removal and minor, negligible entities that do not disrupt the validity of *salat*, reflecting the practical ease (*rukhas*) emphasized in the Ahl al-Bayt's legal methodology.
